title: Highcrest Capital - Dedicated capacity discovery
summary: Initial dedicated capacity discovery for Highcrest Capital. Customer evaluates reserved GPU pools for low latency trading assistant use case; primary concerns are isolation, burst capacity for market open, predictable cost, and SOC2/KMS compliance. Agreed next step: Redwood to run a 2-week benchmark on a 4x-A100 reserved pool with sample prompts and share pricing and security docs.
next_steps: Sofia to send pricing sheet for 4x A100 reserved pool + burst options by 2026-03-06
Arjun to share benchmark template and sample prompt set
Highcrest to provide telemetry sample and list of 3 representative model calls
Schedule 30-min follow-up on results after benchmark (tentative week of 2026-03-23)
action_items: Sofia Lin: send pricing and contract template by 2026-03-06
Arjun Patel: share benchmark plan, scripts, and sample prompts by 2026-03-05
Evan Cho: provide sample telemetry (token counts, QPS) and three representative prompts by 2026-03-06
Priya Nair: confirm minimum security checklist (SOC2 scope, KMS, SSO) by 2026-03-09
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Lin: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we're excited to dig in with Highcrest — i'm Sofia from Redwood, i'm joined by Arjun our SE.
[00:12] Maya Rivera: thanks, Sofia. quick context: we run an internal trading assist and research assistant, want to explore dedicated capacity for latency and data isolation.
[00:28] Arjun Patel: great, can you walk through current stack, models, and peak patterns? even ballpark qps and model sizes helps.
[00:36] Evan Cho: sure, so right now models are a mix — some in-house 13b variants and a tuned 70b open model we serve via a managed endpoint. peak qps at market open is about 350 requests/minute, average request about 180 tokens (prompt + expected generation), latency target 150ms 95th.
[01:02] Liam O'Connell: infra is in GCP, we have private VPCs, strict egress rules. we prefer dedicated GPU pools with no multi-tenant mixing.
[01:15] Sofia Lin: understood. Dedicated (reserved) from Redwood gives you isolated GPU pools in your VPC for predictable throughput; we also do burst capacity to public pools when needed. question: is absolute physical isolation required or logical isolation (no other customers' workloads on same host) sufficient?
[01:36] Priya Nair: we need strong isolation for audit reasons — effectively tenant isolation, dedicated hosts preferred. also SOC2 and key management via our KMS.
[01:46] Arjun Patel: ok, we have an on-prem/private deployment option as well but for dedicated we can provision dedicated hosts (host-level isolation) in the Dedicated offering. there is slight cost premium vs shared dedicated nodes.
[02:05] Maya Rivera: can you describe burst behavior — like at market open we spike 4-5x baseline for ~10 minutes. we want to avoid cold failures but also control cost.
[02:16] Arjun Patel: yes so the typical pattern we recommend: reserved pool sized for baseline throughput + short burst to hosted/backfill capacity. we support configurable burst policies: instant burst to a compatible model variant in public pool or queue with graceful shedding. you can set hard caps to avoid runaway spend.
[02:39] Evan Cho: how does that affect latency — if we burst to public pool we lose isolation and latency can degrade, right?
[02:48] Arjun Patel: that's correct — bursting to hosted/backfill will have slightly higher network latency and possibly different model variant; for market open we can instead recommend a small overprovision (20-30%) plus short-term autoscale ramping to avoid external fallback. we also support pre-warmed replicas for predictable cold- start.
[03:10] Liam O'Connell: what's the typical scaling time to add GPUs? we need to understand autoscale lag.
[03:18] Arjun Patel: in Dedicated: once autoscale triggers we can spin up from spare capacity in the region in ~3-5 minutes for compatible VMs, but host provisioning may be up to 10-12 mins if capacity is not warm. that's why we strongly recommend a burst policy or keeping a buffer pool.
[03:35] Maya Rivera: and pricing model — are we charged for reserved capacity even when idle?
[03:41] Sofia Lin: yes reserved capacity is billed as committed monthly/annual, but we do flexible burst credits and short-term bursting billing models. we can present a couple options in the pricing sheet.
[03:53] Evan Cho: model-wise: we need KV cache and low-latency attention kernels; we do a lot of short responses so throughput per token matters. do you support quantization and kernel optimizations?
[04:04] Arjun Patel: yes, our serving runtime supports int8/4 bit quantization and optimized kernels; there are tradeoffs on quality. we can run comparative benchmarks with your prompts. also we have prefix/KV caching that can lower cost for repeated contexts.
[04:26] Maya Rivera: for compliance: SOC2, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integration are must-haves. also we need to know where logs live and retention.
[04:37] Sofia Lin: we cover SOC2, we integrate with cloud KMS or customer-managed HSM, SSO via SAML, and provide audit logs with configurable retention. we'll share our security pack link (redwood.com/security-docs) — note, transcript may show 'redwood dot com slash secdocs' in our notes.
[04:57] Priya Nair: can you support customer-managed KMS keys in Dedicated?
[05:02] Arjun Patel: yes. Dedicated supports BYOK via KMS and can be configured to only allow decryption within the VPC.
[05:11] Liam O'Connell: any network requirements? egress/open ports? we have strict egress rules so need private connectivity.
[05:18] Sofia Lin: Dedicated can be deployed into your VPC with private peering, no public egress required. for private/on-prem we offer a private control plane option.
[05:30] Maya Rivera: what's the pilot look like? we want a 2-week proof with real load and compare latency/cost.
[05:36] Arjun Patel: typical pilot: provision a 4x-A100 reserved pool (or similar), run a benchmark of representative prompts, compare 95p latency and tokens cost vs current managed endpoint. we provide scripts and help run.
[05:49] Evan Cho: 4x-A100 — will that meet our 150ms 95th?
[05:54] Arjun Patel: depends on model size and sequence length; for the tuned 70b we may need model optimizations or quantized variant to get to 150ms. for smaller 13b variants 150ms 95th is reasonable. benchmark will validate.
[06:10] Maya Rivera: what about model upgrades and rollouts — we need canary and rollback for safety.
[06:16] Arjun Patel: Redwood Console supports canary rollouts, A/B, automatic fallback policies, and tracing to tie regressions to prompts. you'll get per-model dashboards.
[06:28] Liam O'Connell: if we go with dedicated hosts, what's the lead time and contract?
[06:33] Sofia Lin: lead time depends on region capacity; typically 2-4 weeks for dedicated host provisioning after contract. contract terms flexible — monthly or annual commitments with discount tiers.
[06:45] Evan Cho: curious about observability — token-level cost breakdowns, per-route latency, and traces. we need to integrate with our Datadog and internal tracing.
[06:55] Arjun Patel: we have exporters for Datadog and OpenTelemetry hooks; we can push traces and metrics.
[07:03] Maya Rivera: any limitations for on-prem? data residency?
[07:07] Sofia Lin: on-prem/private gives full control — air-gapped version available but will require additional deployment work and support engagement.
[07:15] Priya Nair: encryption in transit and at rest?
[07:18] Arjun Patel: default TLS in transit; at-rest encryption with customer-managed KMS is supported.
[07:25] Evan Cho: can you share an example cost model — tokens vs reserved GPU hours?
[07:31] Sofia Lin: we'll include a cost sheet showing committed GPU pricing, a per-token proxy for hosted fallback, and illustrative run rates based on your sample telemetry.
[07:42] Maya Rivera: ok americans — (laughs) sorry, typo — ok so next step i think is run the benchmark, review security docs, and pricing, then reconvene.
[07:50] Sofia Lin: agreed. we'll set up the benchmark and have Arjun send the scripts.
[07:55] Arjun Patel: i'll also include model variant recommendations, quantization suggestions, and patch notes.
[08:00] Liam O'Connell: on the burst policy, is there a UI to configure thresholds and caps?
[08:05] Arjun Patel: yes Redwood Console has policy editor, you can set caps, fallback target, and circuit-breaker thresholds.
[08:12] Priya Nair: we will need the SOC2 report and network diagram for legal review.
[08:16] Sofia Lin: i'll attach our SOC2 audit summary and network diagram.
[08:20] Maya Rivera: timeline: if benchmark starts week of 3/09 we can review results 3/23 and decide.
[08:25] Sofia Lin: sounds good — we'll aim for that.
[08:28] Evan Cho: one more question — does Redwood provide managed model tuning or do we bring our own tuned weights?
[08:34] Arjun Patel: both — you can bring your tuned model and we can help with performance tuning; we also offer managed fine-tuning services as an add-on.
[08:42] Maya Rivera: ok thanks everyone. we'll await the docs and pricing.
[08:46] Sofia Lin: thanks Highcrest, we'll send follow-ups. bye.

Notes: transcription contains occasional misheard proper nouns (e.g., 'Redwood Reserved' instead of 'Redwood Dedicated'). References to docs: https://redwood.example.com/security-docs, pricing sheet link will be shared in follow-up.
